title: Sindh Workers Children Education Disbursement of Benefits Rules 1976

sections.shortTitle: Sindh Workers Children Education Disbursement of Benefits Rules 1976
sections.section: RULE - Sindh Workers Children (Education) (Disbursement of Benefits) Rules 1976
sections.description:
SIND WORKERS' CHILDREN (EDUCATION) (DISBURSEMENT OF
SIND WORKERS' CHILDREN (EDUCATION) (DISBURSEMENT OF
BENEFITS) RULES, 1976
Sind Govt. Gaz. Pt. IV‑A, 26 Feb. 1976, p. 14.
[No. SO(L‑II)‑2‑7/75.
Rules framed by the Government of Sind in exercise of the powers conferred by
section 6 of the Workers' Children (Education) Ordinance, 1972 (Ordinance XI of
1972) in its application to the Province of Sind.]
1. (1) These rules may be called
the Sind Workers Children (Educa tion) (Disbursement of Benefits) Rules, 1976.
(2) They shall come into force at
once.
2. In these rules, unless the
context otherwise requires :‑
(a) "beneficiary" means one child
of a worker nominated by him for the benefit of free education under the
Ordinance by filling in Part‑I of the form;
(b) "Director" means the Director of Labour, Sind.
(c) "Disbursement Officer" means
an officer appointed as such by Government under rule 9;
(d) "form" means a form appended to these rules;
(e) "Government" means the Government of Sind;
(f) "institution" means a school,
vocational or technical institu tion or other institution run or recognized by
Government for imparting instructions to students of any class from class I to
class X;
(g) "Ordinance" means the Workers'
Children (Education) Ordinance, 1972 (Ordinance XI of 1972).
3. The worker shall be entitled
to re‑imbursement of. the amount, if any, paid by the beneficiary on
account of the admission fee, tuition fee; examination fee and school fund plus
the amount spent on purchase of books, stationery and uniforms up to the
following maximum rates :‑
(a) Rs. 50/‑ per annum if the
beneficiary is studying in any class from class I to class V;
(b) Rs. 75/‑ per annum if the
beneficiary is studying in any class from class VI to class VIII;
(c) Rs. 125/‑ per annum if the, beneficiary is studying in
class IX or class X.
4. (1) The beneficiary shall be
nominated every year and the nomina tion in Part‑I of the form shall be
submitted to the head of the institu tion where such beneficiary is studying.
(2) The head of the institution
shall verify the contents of Part‑I of the form submitted under sub‑rule
(1) by filling the relevant entries in Part‑II of the form and forward
the form to the employer or the manager of the establishment where the worker
is employed.
(3) The employer or manager of
the establishment concerned shall fill in Part‑III if any and forward the
same to the Disbursement Officer by the first week of the month next following,
alongwith a separate list of applicants in duplicate.
5. The Disbursement Officer
shall, on receipt of the form and after necessary scrutiny and checking of the
form as to the eligibility of the worker for the benefit under section d of the
Ordinance arrange that payment in accordance with the provisions of rule 4 to
the employer or manager of the establishment for disbursement to the workers
concerned under intimation to the worker in Part‑IV of the form.
6. Where a beneficiary leaves one
institution for admission to any other institution, the bead of the institution
concerned shall clearly indicate on the school leaving certificate of the
beneficiary that he/she is worker's son/daughter and is eligible for free
education upto Class X and send the necessary intimation to the Disbursement
Officer.
7. The Disbursement Officer shall
furnish an annual consolidated report to the Director in September, each year
showing the amount disburses to the Workers under these rules.
8. The Excise and Taxation
Department shall forward by 3lst July, each year to the Labour Department a
list of establishments assessed to the cess under the Ordinance and payment
made by each establishment.
9. Government may appoint 'as
many officers of the Directorate of Labour Welfare as are necessary for
carrying out the purpose of these rules to be the Disbursement Officers
specifying the areas of their jurisdiction.
